meta.title: Ballade (Op. 100, No. 15 - Opening Dramatic Theme)
meta.composer_source: Study after Friedrich Burgmuller, Op. 100 No. 15

theory.summary: Stormy C-minor 6/8 narrative etude combining a driving compound bass pulse with dramatic melodic leaps.
theory.pattern_tip: Feel 6/8 in two urgent dotted-quarter beats per bar; watch for B-natural leading tones and Ab -> G half-steps.
theory.technique_tip: Keep the repeated left-hand 8th-note chords close to the keys with a firm rhythmic pulse.
theory.ballade_link: Directly anticipates Romantic ballad storytelling and 6/8 dramatic minor-key agitation.
concept_paragraphs: Burgmuller's Ballade in C minor packs theatrical Romantic urgency into a crisp 6/8 pulse: pulsing repeated LH chords propel dramatic RH leaps and urgent half-step sighs (Ab -> G).
In Phrase C (Bars 9-12), notice how Bb7 (V7/III) tears open the storm clouds into noble Eb Major before G7 snaps the drama back to C minor—exact preparation for Chopin's narrative contrasts.

form_map.role: Restless C-minor opening surging through Fm (iv) and G7 back to i.
Intensifies toward an open Dominant G / G7 Half Cadence.
Dramatic relief into Relative Major Eb (III) via Ab and Bb7 (V7/III).
Stormy return closing forcefully onto C minor.

practice_steps: 1. Keep LH repeated 8th-note chords close to the keys with flexible wrist rebound.
2. Feel two urgent dotted-quarter pulses per 6/8 bar ('ONE-two-three, FOUR-five-six').
3. Spot the B-natural leading tone in G7 vs. Bb in Phrase C's Eb-major passage.
4. Build fiery rhythmic control safely from 60% up to 72 BPM.

audio_examples.label: Storm vs. Sanctuary (Cm -> Ab -> Bb7 -> Eb -> G7 -> Cm)
audio_examples.caption: Watch Bb7 open into Eb before G7 pulls back to C minor
